description:
Implement the eight findings agreed during the user's channel-delivery review. Parent: zaq-1lw. This issue authorizes tracking only in this session; no implementation has been performed for these findings.

Baseline: feature commit 14fee186e and https://chatgpt.com/space/page_1e1079bf6234819185ccfa7aecefadc8. The main Channel flow diagram has already been edited for findings 3 and 5; surrounding prose and other diagrams still describe the earlier design. The decisions below supersede those conflicting passages.

## 1. Rename requirements
Rename ZAQ FileRequirements to TransportRequirements, including module/file, types, bridge file_requirements callback to transport_requirements, call sites, tests and documentation. Audit the SDK callback separately: do not silently rename an upstream contract or require dependency publication merely for host naming.

## 2. Unify attachment terminology
Use attachment terminology throughout delivery-domain fields, types and helpers: e.g. files -> attachments and max_files_per_message -> max_attachments_per_message. Audit requirements, plan, steps and reports. Preserve file terminology where it identifies a storage concept, Record kind :file, or provider contract such as Mattermost file_ids. Do not blindly rename inbound/provider APIs.

## 3. Simplify empty-attachment delivery
No outgoing attachments means ordinary text delivery: return the outgoing unchanged from planning and use the normal bridge path. Do not route an empty attachment list through a Channel selection-error policy branch, suppress the Agent's response under stop, or append a duplicate selection notice. AttachDocuments supplies selection failure feedback to the Agent, which composes its response. Audit every attachment_error producer and non-Agent caller before applying this contract; report exceptional paths rather than silently dropping required behavior. No requirements lookup, materialization, plan or executor for ordinary empty-attachment delivery.

## 4. Validate configuration at its owner
Enforce required transport settings and valid values when saving the channel configuration, with actionable field errors and transport-specific requirements. Validate provider-supplied requirements at fetch/normalization boundaries. Planning consumes the validated contract and handles inability to obtain requirements (network/unavailable configuration), not duplicate value validation. Define remediation/migration for existing missing or invalid settings before relying on that invariant; no guessed provider defaults. Actual attachment and encoded payload size checks remain necessary.

## 5. Move materialization into execution
Build the plan from original Record metadata and declared sizes. Keep source Records/handles available to execution, without preloading attachment content just to construct the plan. Materialize required attachments once during execution before adapter upload/send preparation. Validate actual content and exact MIME/multipart payload sizes there. Do not silently send oversized payloads or claim metadata proves encoded size. Explicitly define handling of metadata/actual-size mismatches and groups that no longer fit; do not silently introduce regrouping semantics. Preserve stop guarantees: materialization/preparation failure prevents new publication, and all separate uploads must succeed before publication. Continue records original-index failures and proceeds according to existing policy; no automatic retry. Keep authorization, source preservation, private byte handling and frozen connector identity.

## 6. Consolidate Outgoing delivery data across services
Introduce a typed Outgoing.Delivery (or equivalent nested module under the existing owner):
%Outgoing.Delivery{attachments: [], error: nil, plan: nil}
Replace Outgoing.attachments -> Outgoing.delivery.attachments; attachment_error -> delivery.error; delivery_plan -> delivery.plan. The user explicitly retained the error field: do not remove it based on earlier discussion. Finding 3 governs its treatment on the empty-attachment path.
MANDATORY cross-service impact audit before edits: Agent node produces/consumes attachments, so this is not a Channel-local refactor. Inventory constructors, defaults, type specs, pattern matches, string/atom-key maps, serialization/restoration, Event/NodeRouter boundaries, notifications/workflows, bridges, confirmation/history/public projections, fixtures and tests. Name every affected module and the precise migration in this issue before implementation. Decide compatibility for restored/persisted/old-shape payloads from actual evidence. Shared attachments/error travel as required; plan is created only on Channel, transient, private and stripped before Engine confirmation/persistence. Do not duplicate the authoritative attachment collection in the plan; use stable references. Preserve caller immutability.

Observed direct-reference starting points (not an exhaustive audit):
- lib/zaq/engine/messages/outgoing.ex
- lib/zaq/agent/executor.ex
- lib/zaq/agent/stream_events.ex
- lib/zaq/agent/tools/workflow/run_agent.ex
- lib/zaq/channels/{api,delivery_files,delivery_executor,delivery_confirmation,jido_chat_bridge,email_bridge}.ex
Additional boundaries to inspect: AttachDocuments and NotifyPerson tools/actions; lib/zaq/engine/notifications/notification.ex; channel Bridge/Events/Web message owners; email_bridge/smtp_sender.ex; Engine history/confirmation and all Outgoing.new/builders. A narrow reference search already matched 14 test files; expand by symbols and callers, not just exact field strings.

## 7. Resolve requirements and policy together
Keep failure_policy in DeliveryPlan. Return the resolved policy from the same bridge transport_requirements call as the constraints (TransportRequirements deliberately includes resolved policy). Copy that policy into the immutable plan. Remove redundant separate policy resolution/reads from connection plumbing and planner helpers where superseded. Preserve selected SMTP sender ownership, including IMAP-to-SMTP routing, and frozen connection identity. Current Settings.attachment_failure_policy defaults a missing saved setting to :continue, while planner Map.get(connection, ..., :abort) defaults a missing injected policy to :abort: choose/document one consistent owner/default without silently changing explicit saved false/true behavior. Ordinary empty-attachment delivery must retain its bypass.

## 8. Remove duplicate root state from the plan
Remove DeliveryPlan.root_message_id. Existing thread identity remains owned by Outgoing.thread_id and must not be rewritten during execution. Newly confirmed root election/promotion belongs to separate executor runtime state. Treat Outgoing and the completed plan as immutable inputs; resolve step references against runtime outcomes without editing either. Preserve existing-thread routing, distinction between edited message ID and thread root, continue root promotion after failed/unconfirmed candidates, and no retries.

## Execution and acceptance
Read AGENTS.md and applicable owners: docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md, docs/agent-tools.md, docs/action-reuse.md, docs/conventions.md, docs/code-quality.md, docs/testing-approach.md, docs/documentation.md, docs/services/channels.md, docs/services/engine.md, and Agent harness-critical checks in docs/services/agent.md before affected work. SMTP configuration/UI work also requires system-config guidance, DESIGN.md and BO component rules.

Action reuse assessment: extend existing delivery preparation/execution, Materialization, Bridge and configuration operations; no new agent tools or parallel delivery/configuration paths. Recheck concrete candidates/contracts before implementation and record the per-operation assessment. New nested structs and naming changes are local data-contract work.

Use the existing epic and this issue; do not reimplement the already-closed original plan. Establish a safe migration sequence across producers/consumers. Any unresolved behavior choices (legacy settings, default policy, actual-size mismatch handling, compatibility) must be explicit before coding the dependent change. Reconcile the Page and repository documentation after the final design is settled, without presenting current proposed behavior as already implemented.

Validation must cover real Agent selection -> Outgoing -> Channel -> provider -> Engine paths, ordinary text bypass, nested error preservation, restored constructors, SMTP selected policy, actual-byte/encoded-size boundaries, once-only materialization/execution, stop barriers, continue partial outcomes, root election with immutable inputs, and no private plan/bytes in history/inspection. Reuse existing suites and property tests; retain meaningful authorization and provenance assertions. Disclose concrete existing-test behavior changes and obtain required approval before editing their expectations. Follow issue-level mix q and isolated tests, required review/coverage lifecycle and final mix precommit; feature E2E remains subject to the existing human UX approval gate. No commit/push/publication without authorization.

comments.text: Started from clean feat/channel-files at 14fee186e. User explicitly authorizes implementation of eight findings, superseding tracking-only issue prose. No Git publication authorized. Candidates 9–14 excluded.

Cross-service impact audit (before source edits), baseline 14fee186e; findings 1–8 only.

Ownership/contracts: StreamEvents owns per-request selection; Executor composes the pipeline result; Engine.Messages.Outgoing owns canonical delivery data; Channel owns the transient plan; DeliveryExecutor owns acquired bytes, prepared requests, results and elected roots; Engine history owns persisted confirmation. Source Records remain authoritative in Outgoing.delivery.attachments, referenced by original index in plans. Outgoing and completed plan remain immutable executor inputs.

Agent: migrate StreamEvents result/default/state types and selection producer/consumer to Delivery; Executor.normalize result forwards typed delivery; Outgoing.from_pipeline_result copies delivery and strips all atom/string delivery/legacy private metadata keys. AttachDocuments destination-preflight Outgoing constructor moves Records to Delivery; its validated Action, reduce_selection, provenance, actor and destination preflight remain shared. RunAgent.handle_response reads delivery.error and delivery.attachments but retains public workflow output attachments: signed Record.metadata. RunAgent fails rejected selection before NotifyPerson; no non-Agent selection-error producer found. Agent.Api, RequestControl, Status default/queued/failure constructors use Outgoing defaults and preserve typed delivery through copies/return hops.

Engine: Notifications.deliver builder wraps Notification.attachments in Delivery. Notification.build restores signed atom/string-key Record maps through existing Record Zoi validation; NotifyPerson and workflow persisted attachments output/input remain unchanged. No persisted or JSON-encoded Outgoing format found; Event/NodeRouter transport canonical structs. Keep legacy atom/string pipeline-result attachments/attachment_error ingestion only at Outgoing builder for restored integrations; never accept an incoming plan. Canonical live Outgoing fields change atomically; mixed-version Erlang nodes require coordinated deployment, no parallel top-level fields. Events upsert_outgoing and Api.map_to_upsert_outgoing are text constructors using default Delivery. Api outgoing Event selectors remain canonical struct boundaries.

Channel: Bridge ZAQ callback, JidoChatBridge and EmailBridge rename to transport_requirements, return validated requirements AND resolved failure_policy; keep upstream adapter.file_requirements/1, SDK max_files_per_post/max_file_size and provider uploaded_files/file_ids unchanged. Settings remains policy owner, default continue; selected SMTP settings own policy, including IMAP routing. Remove duplicate connection policy injection. Api, DeliveryFiles (rename DeliveryAttachments), DeliveryExecutor and both bridges use nested Delivery. Planner validates Record metadata/declared sizes without content acquisition or provider preparation. Execution calls existing Materialization and validated DecodeBase64 once per eligible index, then validates actual fixed groups and exact encoded payloads before adapter effects. Stop preparation barrier and all-upload barrier remain. Continue keeps original-index errors, no retries or regrouping. DeliveryPlan/Step rename delivery-domain files/refs, remove duplicated source collection and root_message_id; existing Outgoing.thread_id initializes separate runtime root state. Bridge operation inputs rename files to attachments, preserving SDK field translation.

Privacy/projections: DeliveryConfirmation strips plan, clears confirmed Record content and filters original indices before Engine.Events record_delivery_confirmation; Delivery and plan Inspect omit private payloads. Engine.History.Delivery and CommunicationPolicy use receipts/safe metadata rather than Outgoing delivery fields. MessageFormatter, EventNames, WebBridge and Web.Message inbound attachments remain their existing contracts; inspect text/status paths for accidental delivery leakage. SmtpSender consumes prepared attachment transport maps, not Outgoing, and retains provider payload terminology.

Configuration: extend existing EmailConfig changeset, Engine.ChannelConfig persistence validation, EmailConnectorSettings.save/form projection and SmtpSettings key access. Save new max_attachments_per_message; read legacy max_files_per_message without inventing limits. Enabled SMTP saves require count/encoded-byte limits; disabled drafts may omit them; malformed explicit values rejected. Existing invalid/missing legacy settings remain readable for text and must be corrected on next enabled save; attachment requirements fail closed at normalization. Jido provider limits validated at normalization, not again in planning.

Tests: direct contract suites engine/messages/outgoing_test; agent stream_events/executor/tools/workflow/run_agent tests; channels delivery_files (rename delivery_attachments), attachment_policy, delivery_executor, api, outbound_connection, jido_chat_delivery, delivery_confirmation, email_bridge/outgoing_attachments, email_confirmation_integration, email_file_delivery_integration, disk_file_delivery_integration, attachment_agent_journey; Engine notification/workflow/history suites and enabled SMTP save fixtures. Preserve authorization/provenance and source-preservation assertions; add normalization/immutability/index properties and execution-path integration coverage. Test behavior migrations explicitly approved by user via asynchronous questions: empty-error text bypass; acquisition/exact sizing/failures move to executor; policy moves to requirements/plan; fixed metadata groups may fail actual encoded checks without regrouping; missing declared sizes remain eligible; size drift is accepted only within actual fixed-group bounds; enabled SMTP fixtures supply limits and legacy reading remains supported.

Action reuse assessment: delivery planning/execution EXTEND DeliveryFiles/DeliveryExecutor and Bridge operations, local orchestration only (not independently composable tool actions). Acquisition REUSE Materialization.materialize and Jido.Exec.run(DecodeBase64), preserve trusted context and existing source authorization. Notification/workflow delivery REUSE NotifyPerson -> Notifications -> Channels.Events -> Api, preserve NodeRouter/StepRunner. Configuration EXTEND EmailConnectorSettings/SaveEmailConnector and ChannelConfig changesets, no parallel save path. Nested Delivery/requirements/group refs are LOCAL-ONLY data contracts, no new agent tools or Actions. Verify by real storage/agent/provider/Engine suites plus focused properties.

Sequence: (1) shared Delivery plus Agent/Engine/Channel producer-consumer migration and naming; (2) requirements/policy and config owners; (3) metadata-only planning and runtime preparation/root state; (4) approved test migrations and regressions; (5) issue mix q/isolated tests/self-review and docs. Existing epic UX .10 -> E2E .11 -> review .12 -> coverage .13 gates remain; do not self-approve or close pending human gates. No application commit/push/publication.
